brief.recommendation: Waiting costs ~$305,379 (996s remaining at $18,400/min) and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance (BIZ-5). Termination requires Loyalty & Rewards approval due to active change-calendar window CHG-7104 with policy=consult_owner (BIZ-3). Human owner must decide between accepting 20-min replay cost or continued checkout degradation.

audit.report: A loyalty tier recalculation batch job (batch_replayable_loyalty_tier_recalc, pid 1450988) held an idle transaction for 4.2 seconds during a peak-season freeze, blocking checkout and driving success to 0% over 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The database guardian initially proposed waiting since the blocker had only run 4.2s and the business tolerates 60s of degradation, but trade-off analysis showed the job had ~996s remaining and waiting would cost ~$305,379 — far exceeding the tolerance window. Termination requires Loyalty & Rewards approval due to active change calendar CHG-7104 (holiday tier migration, policy=consult_owner). Both guardians escalated to the human owner after one 164-second round; no automatic action was taken.
audit.root_cause: The loyalty_tier_recalc batch job (pid 1450988) held an idle transaction open for 4.2s during peak-season freeze, blocking checkout sessions and causing 0% success rate with $18,400/min revenue at risk.
lessons: For loyalty_tier_recalc workload: Add a pre-flight check for active change calendar windows (like CHG-7104) before allowing batch jobs to run during peak freeze periods, since interruption requires owner consultation.
For loyalty_tier_recalc workload: Configure an automatic termination timeout aligned with the 60s business tolerance rather than relying on guardian negotiation, since waiting 996s costs ~$305K.
For loyalty_tier_recalc workload: Ensure batch jobs use shorter transactions or checkpointing to reduce lock hold time during peak periods, since a 4.2s idle transaction blocked checkout.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian wasted no rounds — it proposed WAIT initially but immediately investigated and switched to ESCALATE after seeing trade-off analysis (BIZ-5) showing waiting cost $305K and exceeded the 60s tolerance. Both guardians correctly identified the change calendar constraint (CHG-7104, consult_owner) and escalated to the human owner without overriding the invariant.
follow_ups: Loyalty & Rewards team to decide: accept 20-minute replay cost of loyalty_tier_recalc or tolerate extended checkout degradation.
Review why loyalty_tier_recalc was running during peak-season freeze despite active CHG-7104 change calendar window.
Implement automated guardrail to prevent batch_replayable jobs from running during freeze windows without explicit approval.

Checkout will remain degraded until a decision is made, but the business tolerance window is already exceeded, so immediate human intervention is required.
proposal.risk_assessment: If escalation is delayed, checkout may continue to lose revenue at the current rate (~$305k per 996s wait). If termination proceeds without owner approval, it may violate the consult_owner policy and risk demoting customers during holiday tier migration. If wait continues beyond 60s, the SLO breach and revenue loss exceed tolerated limits.
